plan.lspNative.title: Native LSP and completion workflow
plan.lspNative.description: Checks real NVDA output, held Braille information, and perceptible menu interaction; LSP content and event sequences already have automated coverage.
plan.lspNative.context: You are in the test Neovim in the original Windows Terminal tab. The Python file lsp_features.py is open. Press Escape once; you are then in Normal mode and cannot insert stray characters.
plan.lspNative.status.title: Report the active LSP clearly
plan.lspNative.status.action: After claiming with F12, press F1, wait for all NVDA speech, then press Escape and F10.
plan.lspNative.status.expected: NVDA clearly reports that Pyright is active for the Python buffer. It does not expose a raw Lua or protocol representation.
plan.lspNative.automaticParameters.title: Track the active parameter while typing
plan.lspNative.automaticParameters.conte: You are in the test Neovim in the original Windows Terminal tab. The Python file lsp_features.py is open. For this task, F3 places the cursor inside a prepared empty calculate_total() call and enters Insert mode automatically.
plan.lspNative.automaticParameters.actio: After claiming with F12, press Escape once and then F3. Slowly type exactly 3.5, 2, 0.1, waiting for speech after the opening parenthesis and after each comma. Next press Ctrl+Left three times: the cursor returns from the third to the second and finally to the already filled first argument. Press Left and Right once within that first argument. If a Braille display is present, observe whether it continues to show source text instead of the automatic hint. Then press Escape and F10.
plan.lspNative.automaticParameters.expec: On entering the call, NVDA reports the price parameter; after the commas it reports quantity and discount. Returning to the already filled first argument speaks price again, while merely pressing Left or Right within the same argument remains silent. Every necessary announcement follows without disruptive delay, contains no raw LSP or Lua representation, and does not interrupt typing. The automatic hint is speech-only and does not replace source text on the Braille display.
plan.lspNative.parameters.title: Hold function parameters on Braille
plan.lspNative.parameters.context: You are in the test Neovim in the original Windows Terminal tab. The cursor is already on the function name calculate_total. Press Escape once and do not move the cursor.
plan.lspNative.parameters.action: After claiming with F12, hold NVDA, briefly press Space, and release only Space. Keep NVDA held: verify that only signature 1 with its documentation appears first, then use the display's normal forward/back controls to page once through that information and return to its start. Slowly press l three times; the first press must show parameter 1, followed by parameters 2 and 3. Press j once and verify that only signature 2 with its documentation appears. Press l twice so parameter 1 and then parameter 2 appear. Press k once: signature 1 must appear without a parameter; a following l must show parameter 1 again despite its previous position and must not continue at parameter 3. Press j again and then h: even in the backward direction, parameter 1 of signature 2 must appear first instead of its previously selected parameter 2. Release NVDA and repeat the same held query once without moving the cursor. Then release NVDA. Press F4 once; after the message, the cursor is on the opening parenthesis. Invoke the held query there once and release NVDA. Press F4 again; the cursor is now on the closing parenthesis. Invoke the query there once as well and release NVDA. Then press Escape and F10.
plan.lspNative.parameters.expected: Speech says signature, parameter, and documentation in full. On Braille, signatures start compactly with S 1 of 2 or S 2 of 2, parameters with P 1 of 3 through P 3 of 3, and documentation with D:. The calculate_total function name and the price, quantity, and discount parameter names remain complete. The initial view and j/k show only the selected signature with documentation; h/l shows only one of its parameters. After the initial view and every signature change, the first h or l press always shows parameter 1 of the selected signature, regardless of the previous parameter position or direction. Only subsequent presses move forward or backward. Paging keeps the current signature information on the Braille display; source text returns only after NVDA is released. The immediate repeated query and the queries on the opening and closing parentheses provide the same structured signatures and parameters; the query does not move the real cursor.
plan.lspNative.completion.title: Operate and perceive native completion
plan.lspNative.completion.context: You are in the test Neovim in the original Windows Terminal tab. Press Escape once. F3 moves to a prepared completion location and enters Insert mode automatically.
plan.lspNative.completion.action: After claiming with F12, press F3 and then F5. Continue with Ctrl+N beyond calculate_total, calculate_tax, and calculate_tip: after the last candidate, reach the state with no selected completion once, then candidate 1 on the next press. Move back at least once with Ctrl+P, accept a function with Ctrl+Y, and read the resulting line and the character at the cursor. If audio was answered Yes at startup, also listen for the opening sound and the distinct closing sound caused by acceptance. Then press Escape and F10.
plan.lspNative.completion.expected: The menu contains at least the three prepared suggestions calculate_total, calculate_tax, and calculate_tip. NVDA reports selected suggestions clearly. The step between the last and first candidate explicitly reports that no completion is selected; it is not silent. Navigation and acceptance respond smoothly and without disruptive repetition. The accepted function gains exactly one pair of parentheses and the cursor is between them. When audio is available, menu open and menu close each sound exactly once and are clearly distinct; without declared audio, only the other perception is assessed.
plan.diagnostics.title: Diagnostic output and earcons
plan.diagnostics.description: Checks perceptible Ruff diagnostics, navigation, sounds, and physical Braille persistence. Ranges, sources, and jump targets also have automated coverage.
plan.diagnostics.context: You are in the test Neovim in the original Windows Terminal tab. diagnostics.py is open and the cursor is already on the unused import path on line one; sep on the same line is unused as well. Press Escape once and do not move the cursor yet.
plan.diagnostics.navigation.title: Speak, navigate, and perceive diagnostics
plan.diagnostics.navigation.action: After claiming with F12, press F6 and wait until “Diagnostics ready” is announced. F6 reliably places the cursor on the first Ruff test diagnostic. Only then press F7; it reports the Ruff F401 warning at the cursor. Slowly press F9 repeatedly and follow “number of total” until the Ruff F821 error for missing_name and, after the last diagnostic, the first one are reached. Press F8 once to move backwards to the last diagnostic. If audio was answered Yes at startup, compare the warning and error sounds. Finally press F5: the cursor automatically moves to a prepared clean position and Access Link explicitly queries a diagnostic there. Then press Escape and F10.
plan.diagnostics.navigation.expected: Immediately after the readiness announcement, F7 clearly reports the unused-import diagnostic without a prior diagnostic jump. F9 reaches every announced number, including multiple diagnostics at the same position, and then wraps to the first; F8 moves backwards to the last. Every key press produces exactly one complete announcement without disruptive delay. When audio is available, F401 uses the warning sound and F821 the clearly different error sound; every jump to a warning or error produces exactly one matching diagnostic sound without disruptive overlap. Information and hints remain soundless as in VS Code. F5 reports “no diagnostic” and confirms this explicit empty query with a third, short, clearly distinct diagnostic sound; mere cursor movement across clean lines remains silent. Without declared audio, only the other perception is assessed. Together with completion, all five distinct sounds are covered when audio is available: menu open, menu close, warning, error, and no diagnostic.
plan.diagnostics.held.title: Hold a diagnostic on Braille
plan.diagnostics.held.action: After claiming with F12, press F6, wait for “Diagnostics ready”, and only then press F7. Next hold NVDA and Shift, briefly press Space, and release only Space and Shift. Keep NVDA held: press j once and then k once to switch between the F401 diagnostics for path and sep and back. Finally release NVDA, then press Escape and F10.
plan.diagnostics.held.expected: The two distinct F401 diagnostics for path and sep are readable on Braille while the gesture is held and change with j/k. Releasing it restores the previous Braille output.
plan.focus.title: Focus isolation and fail-open behavior
plan.focus.description: Checks actual Windows Terminal ownership and return to normal terminal behavior, which test doubles cannot reproduce completely.
plan.focus.workflow.title: Distinguish claimed and unclaimed terminal tabs
plan.focus.context: You initially are in the test Neovim in the original Windows Terminal tab. Press Escape, claim exactly this tab with F12, and leave Neovim open. The middle part needs a second Windows Terminal tab showing an ordinary PowerShell prompt.
plan.focus.workflow.action: Use the plus button or profile menu to open a second Windows Terminal tab with PowerShell. Do not start Neovim or press F12 there. Check ordinary input and navigation without submitting a command. Return to the original tab, press Escape and F10 in Neovim, then check ordinary input and navigation again in the PowerShell view that reappears there.
plan.focus.workflow.expected: The second unclaimed tab keeps NVDA's normal terminal behavior and receives no Neovim output from the first tab. After F10, PowerShell in the original tab is immediately usable normally as well; no Braille output is stuck and input is not blocked.
plan.completionPlugin.context: You are in the test Neovim in the original Windows Terminal tab. The Python file is open. Press Escape once. F3 moves to a prepared completion location and enters Insert mode automatically.
plan.nvimCmp.title: Optional nvim-cmp compatibility
plan.nvimCmp.description: A short reality check of the automatically tested adapter API with NVDA and Windows Terminal.
plan.nvimCmp.menu.title: Operate and perceive nvim-cmp suggestions
plan.nvimCmp.menu.action: After claiming with F12, press F3 and F5, select at least calculate_total, calculate_tax, and calculate_tip with Ctrl+N, move back with Ctrl+P, and accept with Ctrl+Y. Read the resulting line and the character at the cursor. If audio was answered Yes at startup, listen for exactly one opening sound and the distinct closing sound caused by acceptance. Merely moving between suggestions is not intended to produce another sound. Then press Escape and F10.
plan.nvimCmp.menu.expected: The menu contains at least the three prepared suggestions. NVDA clearly reports selected nvim-cmp suggestions; navigation and acceptance remain smooth, and internal tables are not spoken. As in the other two test profiles, the accepted function gains exactly one pair of parentheses and the cursor is between them. This alignment belongs only to the isolated test configuration; automatic parentheses are not built into a user's nvim-cmp setup and normally require additional configuration. When audio is available, opening and closing each produce exactly one suitable, distinct menu sound; individual selection changes remain silent like NVDA's suggestion feedback. Without declared audio, only the other perception is assessed.
plan.blinkCmp.title: Optional blink.cmp compatibility
plan.blinkCmp.description: A short reality check of the automatically tested adapter API with NVDA and Windows Terminal.
plan.blinkCmp.menu.title: Operate and perceive blink.cmp suggestions
plan.blinkCmp.menu.action: After claiming with F12, press F3 and F5, select at least calculate_total, calculate_tax, and calculate_tip with Ctrl+N, move back with Ctrl+P, and accept a function with Ctrl+Y. Read the resulting line and the character at the cursor. If audio was answered Yes at startup, listen for exactly one opening sound and the distinct closing sound caused by acceptance. Merely moving between suggestions is not intended to produce another sound. Then press Escape and F10.
plan.blinkCmp.menu.expected: The menu contains at least the three prepared suggestions. NVDA clearly reports selected blink.cmp suggestions; navigation and acceptance remain smooth, and internal tables are not spoken. As in the other two test profiles, the accepted function gains exactly one pair of parentheses and the cursor is between them. Blink provides this through its built-in auto-brackets feature. When audio is available, opening and closing each produce exactly one suitable, distinct menu sound; individual selection changes remain silent like NVDA's suggestion feedback. Without declared audio, only the other perception is assessed.
plan.cDiagnostics.title: C diagnostic with Clang-Tidy
plan.cDiagnostics.description: A short compatibility check that a real C diagnostic from nvim-lint is presented clearly, independently of Python.
plan.cDiagnostics.context: You are in the test Neovim in the original Windows Terminal tab. diagnostics.c is open and the cursor is on missing_first. Press Escape once and do not move the cursor yet.
plan.cDiagnostics.presentation.title: Perceive a Clang-Tidy diagnostic
plan.cDiagnostics.presentation.action: After claiming with F12, first press F2: the repeated task must start with test ID D3. Then press F6 and wait for “Diagnostics ready”; F6 places the cursor on the first real Clang-Tidy test diagnostic. Press F7, then F9 for the second diagnostic, and F9 once more to wrap to the first. Finally press F8 once to move backwards to the second diagnostic again. When audio is available, listen for the error sound at every diagnostic. Then press Escape and F10.
plan.cDiagnostics.presentation.expected: F2 clearly identifies D3. F7 reports missing_first as “1 of 2”. F9 reaches missing_second as “2 of 2” and then “1 of 2” again; F8 moves backwards to “2 of 2”. Each real Clang-Tidy error is reported clearly and exactly once per key press; its source and position are meaningful. With audio, each diagnostic produces exactly one error sound without disruptive delay.
plan.markdownDiagnostics.title: Markdown diagnostic with markdownlint
plan.markdownDiagnostics.description: A short compatibility check that a real Markdown warning from nvim-lint is presented clearly.
plan.markdownDiagnostics.context: You are in the test Neovim in the original Windows Terminal tab. diagnostics.md is open and the cursor is on the second level-one heading. Press Escape once and do not move the cursor yet.
plan.markdownDiagnostics.presentation.ac: After claiming with F12, press F6 and wait for “Diagnostics ready”; F6 places the cursor on the real markdownlint test diagnostic. Then press F7, followed by F9 once. When audio is available, listen for the warning sound. Then press Escape and F10.
plan.markdownDiagnostics.presentation.ex: F7 and F9 each report the real markdownlint MD025 warning for the second heading clearly and exactly once; its source and position are meaningful. With audio, each query produces exactly one warning sound without disruptive delay.
